newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INTERVIEW-Eureko would use debt, equity to buy GAN.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Eureko would use debt, equity to buy GAN.

text.p: Eureko, an alliance of six European financial services companies, said its members would pay with both loans and new shares if it succeeds in acquiring French state-controlled insurer GAN.
"It will be a combination of equity and debt," said Jeff Medlock, managing director of Eureko.
Medlock said debt would be required as bridging capital ahead of the intended listing of Eureko about two years time.
He said Eureko aims to list 49-50 percent of the total group in Amsterdam, Paris and, probably, London.
Eureko said on Tuesday it had proposed an acquisition plan which would leave the French insurance company intact and see Eureko jump from the seventh to the third biggest insurance group in Europe.

He said it was impossible to say yet how much Eureko would be willing to pay for GAN. He added Eureko was looking for a 100 percent stake in GAN and it would not be interested in sharing a holding in the French insurer.
"It depends on the offer the French government is making, the approval from Brussels for a refinance scheme and the question also of how large GAN's debts are," Medlock said.

GAN lost 5.7 billion French francs last year because of bad property deals. The previous conservative French government announced in February a 20 billion franc rescue package, but this still awaits approval by the European Commission.
"The question is whether GAN has brought the value of its debt to true value," Medlock said.
He said GAN's problems lay only on the property side and that its underlying business and network were good.
"GAN is big in a very important market... and France is the biggest market in Europe we are not yet represented," he said.
GAN is also strong in Britain and active in Canada, the United States, Portugal, Switzerland, Spain and has a shareholding in Italian insurer SAI.
"Eureko and GAN are quite complementory," Medlock said, explaining a merger would combine Eureko's strengths in northern Europe with those of GAN in the south.
Eureko aims to have established a firm base throughout Europe by the turn of the century.
"Europe is our main aim," Medlock said.
And if the GAN takeover did not work out, he said Eureko would seek other European partners.
"We have had several approaches and currently we are talking to a company in Switzerland and in Italy," Medlock said.
Eureko also has ambitions towards the United States and, in the longer run, Asia.
The current Eureko partners are Dutch Achmea, Portuguese BCP/Atlantico, Britain's Friends Provident, Gothaer of Germany, Denmark's Topdanmark and Wasa of Sweden.
Medlock said all members except Topdanmark would be able to participate in the financing of the acquisition.
"Topdanmark is supportive of the route we are mapping out, but they have their (financial) limitations," he said.
In 1996, the Eureko alliance had turnover of 43 billion guilders.
Medlock said the alliance was also well this year.
"Results in the first quarter were well above the budget," he said, adding the second quarter appeared to be even better.
